items.root_cause: The ask ledger and its size-conflict park are keyed by product id alone, while a refusal belongs to one work entry (name+size). The work list binds a stale no-id row to its same-name sibling's product id by the name-only link match (lines 1621-1622), so one pid carries two work entries of different sizes; Update-HyVeeAskLedger then records the first entry's size, not the refused entry's, and Test-HyVeeAskParked parks the entry that does NOT conflict. Any product Hy-Vee re-sized since July, whose old-size row is still carried, lands in this state.

surface_fix.what: Test-HyVeeAskParked returns '' (not parked) for a size-conflict entry whose recorded size equals its recorded theirs (ordinal, trimmed): that entry is self-contradictory. Unparks the 7 persisted entries with no data edit.
surface_fix.exact_change: in Test-HyVeeAskParked, inside the size-conflict branch and before the ordinal size compare: if ([string]::Equals(([string]$Entry['size']).Trim(), ([string]$Entry['theirs']).Trim(), [StringComparison]::Ordinal)) { return '' }

root_fix.what: (1) The work list never binds a no-id row to a product id by NAME ALONE when that link's exact name+size key is itself a row in the previous file: the product already has its own row at the link's size, so the stale twin keeps pid 0, is carried unasked and ages out at as_of+90 (2026-10-13 to 2026-10-18 for the 10 twins). (2) Update-HyVeeAskLedger records the REFUSED entry's own size: Invoke-HyVeeWorkPass adds ours = $size to each SizeConflictRows entry (line 784) and line 417 prefers it over $sizeByPid for a size-conflict outcome. (3) Correct the stale comment at line 880 ('under the 14-day rotation'; RotationDays is the 90-day quarter).
root_fix.where: grocery/pull-regular-hyvee.ps1: work-list build lines 1601-1625 (collect the prev-row name|size keys first, then skip the $byNm bind when $idByName holds that name at a size that is itself a prev-row key); Invoke-HyVeeWorkPass line 784; Update-HyVeeAskLedger line 417; comment line 880
root_fix.exact_change: before the foreach at 1601 build $prevKeys = @{} of name|size for every prev row; in the else branch at 1620-1623, bind from $byNm[0] only when -not $prevKeys.ContainsKey($byNm[0].nm + '|' + <that link's size key>) (the developer reads the size half of the $idByName key it matched); line 784 adds ours = [string]$size; line 417: size = if ($outc -eq $script:HvSizeConflictReason -and $oursByPid.ContainsKey($p)) { $oursByPid[$p] } else { [string]$sizeByPid[$p] }

THE TRAP IN THE QUEUE'S OWN FIX SHAPE: widening the 9459a1 branch as written calls Resolve-MultibuyPackCount, which reads counts with Get-PackCount and takes the HIGH end of a range, while the plain each path reads Get-EachPackCount and takes the least favourable LOW end (aa28983df). Measured: tortillas would read /30 (0.0833, not 0.125), King's Hawaiian /12 (0.3333, not 0.6667), Sunbelt /10 (0.25, not 0.3125), and two of those would take their store's cell at an understated price (dinner-rolls|Hy-Vee 0.4158 -> 0.3333, granola-bars|Fareway 0.288 -> 0.25).
items.root_cause: The each branch of Get-UnitPrice has two count readers and a price-shape allow-list. The plain path divides with Get-EachPackCount; the multibuy path (9459a1) divides with Resolve-MultibuyPackCount, which reads Get-PackCount and so ignores the least-favourable-range rule; and only a Buy-N-Get-K price text (Test-IsMultibuy) reaches the dividing path at all. Every other non-plain shape ('N for $M', '2/ $5.00', '(2/$5)' in a name) with a stated count falls to 'per-each' and ships the package price as one unit.

surface_fix.what: divide a stated pack count for every non-plain price on an each-unit commodity, not only Buy-N-Get-K
surface_fix.exact_change: line 1124: if ((-not $plain) -and (Test-IsMultibuy ([string]$deal.price_text))) becomes if (-not $plain); the basis string at 1127 names the shape: 'per-N-pack (non-plain, count from ...)'. Update the comment block at 1113-1123 to drop the 'left for their own item' paragraph.

root_fix.what: ONE count reader for the each branch: Resolve-MultibuyPackCount reads each party with Get-EachPackCount instead of Get-PackCount, so a count range ('6 to 12 ct', '8-10 ct', '20 or 30 ct') takes its least favourable end on every path and a conflict between parties is still refused. Measured: this changes the count of 0 existing Buy-N-Get-K rows on candidates-2026-09-28.
root_fix.exact_change: replace the three Get-PackCount calls in Resolve-MultibuyPackCount with Get-EachPackCount. Before shipping, run ops/count-source-lifters.ps1 -Script grocery/pricing-math-lib.ps1 and grep Resolve-MultibuyPackCount across grocery/ and ops/ (compare-deals.ps1 holds 1 reference): every caller must want the each reading, or gets its own function.

items.subject: Triage residual: Sam's weight-first pack total vs pieces needs a reading rule (dc1b5b residual 6)
evidence: Over 24 Sam's deal files (grocery/out/sams/sams-deals-2026-09-*.json), 993 distinct names carry the weight-first shape '<weight>, N pk/ct'; 966 carry Sam's own unit price (field sams_unit_price). Of the 639 whose unit price is per weight: 616 (96%) reproduce the PIECES reading the engine uses, 23 reproduce the TOTAL reading, 27 have no unit price, the rest are '/ea'.

Sam's own unit price is NOT a sound oracle, which rules out options A and C as written: among the 23 TOTAL matches are rows where Sam's divided by ONE piece, e.g. 'Barilla Pasta Rotini & Farfalle, Variety Pack, 1 lb., 6 pk.' $8.52 at 53.3 cents/oz (six 1 lb boxes are 8.9 cents/oz), 'Sunlee Coconut Milk 13.5 oz., 6 pk.' $11.48 at 85.0 cents/fl oz, 'Nate's Honey ... 16 oz., 2 pk.' $9.98 at $0.62/oz.
